title: Heaps & Priority Queues
syllabus_note: Additional DS Concept (Foundational extension beyond prescribed lab syllabus)
definition: A Heap is a specialized complete binary tree-based data structure that satisfies the heap property: in a Min-Heap, the key at the root is the minimum among all keys, and in a Max-Heap, the key at the root is the maximum.

heap_types.min_heap: Parent node key <= child node keys. Root is the global minimum.
heap_types.max_heap: Parent node key >= child node keys. Root is the global maximum.

Operating system process scheduling by priority

viva_questions.question: What is the difference between a Binary Search Tree and a Binary Heap?
viva_questions.answer: A BST maintains an in-order sorted relationship where left < root < right. A Heap only maintains the heap order property (root is min or max of its subtree) and must be a complete binary tree, enabling compact array storage.

viva_questions.question: Why is array representation preferred for binary heaps?
viva_questions.answer: Because a heap is always a complete binary tree, it has no missing nodes between indices 0 and size - 1. Pointers are not required, saving memory and providing exceptional cache locality.
